title: Review: Scalars and vectors; Describing motion; Kinematics with calculus; Motion graphs; Constant-acceleration equations; Reference frames and relative motion; Projectile motion; Systems and center of mass
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics C: Mechanics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: MS05-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; MS05-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; MS05-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; K02-1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: D07-1#N.9, K01-1#N.10, K03-1#N.5b, K05-1#N.3, K06-calc-1#N.4, MS05-1#N.13, D07-1#N.7, K01-1#N.2, K03-1#N.16, K05-1#N.16a, K06-calc-1#N.11, MS05-1#N.4. assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Scalar
items.clue: Quantity with magnitude only, such as speed, mass or energy.

items.label: Vector
items.clue: Quantity with magnitude and direction, such as force or momentum.

items.label: Components
items.clue: Two perpendicular parts that together replace the original arrow.

items.label: Acceleration
items.clue: Gradient of a velocity–time graph; uniform when the line is straight.

questions.stem: A diver makes two dives from the same springboard. In each dive, her center of mass leaves the board from the same height with the same velocity. In dive 1 she keeps her body straight; in dive 2 she pulls into a tight tuck soon after leaving the board. Air resistance is negligible. How do the maximum heights reached by her center of mass in the two dives compare?

options.text: Dive 2's is greater, since pulling into a tuck lifts her body higher.
They cannot be compared, since a rotating object is not a projectile.
They are equal, since her center of mass moves as a projectile in both dives.
Dive 1's is greater, since her outstretched body reaches higher.

questions.stem: A car travels 3.0 km along a straight road at a constant speed of 10 m s⁻¹, then returns along the same road to its starting point at a constant speed of 15 m s⁻¹. What are its average speed and its average velocity for the whole journey?

options.text: Average speed 12.5 m s⁻¹; average velocity 0 m s⁻¹
Average speed 12 m s⁻¹; average velocity 0 m s⁻¹
Average speed 12 m s⁻¹; average velocity 12 m s⁻¹
Average speed 12 m s⁻¹; average velocity −2.5 m s⁻¹

questions.stem: A car travelling at 16 m s⁻¹ brakes with uniform deceleration and comes to rest in 4.0 s. What distance does the car travel while braking?
questions.explanation: The acceleration is constant, so the average velocity is halfway between 16 m s⁻¹ and 0: 8.0 m s⁻¹. Δx = 8.0 × 4.0 = 32 m. The same answer follows from Δx = v_x0 t + ½a_x t² with a_x = −4.0 m s⁻²: 64 − 32 = 32 m.

questions.stem: A cyclist rides east at 6 m s⁻¹ relative to the road. Observer X stands beside the road. Observer Y is in a car that moves east along the same road at a constant 10 m s⁻¹. Which statement correctly compares the cyclist's velocity as measured by Y with the velocity measured by X?

options.text: Y measures the same velocity as X does, 6 m s⁻¹ east along the road.
Y measures a smaller speed than X does, and in the opposite direction.
Y measures a larger speed than X does, and in the same direction.
Y measures a smaller speed than X does, in the same direction.

questions.stem: An object moves along the x-axis with velocity v_x(t) = (2.0 m s⁻³)t² − (2.0 m s⁻²)t. What is its acceleration a_x at t = 2.0 s?
A robot vacuum moves 1.1 m east and then 1.6 m north, each along a straight line. What is the magnitude of its displacement from its starting point?
A uniform rod of mass 2m and length L has a small ball of mass m fixed to one end. How far from the other end of the rod is the centre of mass of the rod–ball system?

A runner moves along a straight track. Her position x is measured from a marker on the track. She starts at x = +30 m, runs to x = +70 m, then turns around and runs to x = −20 m, where she stops. What is her displacement?
A toy car is released from rest on a straight slope and speeds up with constant acceleration. It travels 0.60 m in the first 2.0 s. How far does it travel between t = 4.0 s and t = 6.0 s?

A moving walkway in an airport moves at constant velocity v_W relative to the floor. A passenger walks on the walkway with velocity v_P relative to the walkway. A worker walks on the floor beside the walkway at constant velocity v_F relative to the floor. All three velocities are components along the same straight line. Which expression gives the passenger's velocity as measured by the worker?
An object moves along the x-axis with acceleration a_x(t) = kt, where k is a positive constant. At t = 0 it is at x = 0 with velocity v₀. What is its position x(t)?

A hiker walks 5 m east and then 9 m west along a straight path. Student 1 takes east as the positive direction; Student 2 takes west as the positive direction. Each finds the hiker's resultant displacement as a signed component. Which statement correctly compares their results?

options.text: Only Student 1 can be right, as east has to be the positive direction.
Student 1 gets −4 m and Student 2 gets +4 m, and both results mean 4 m west.
Both get +4 m, by subtracting the smaller distance from the larger.
Both get 14 m, since the two walks simply add to give the resultant.
